newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government has no choice but to float the baht and the move is further evidence of policy inconsistencies, the Democrat leader says. During last week's budget debate, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh pledged the baht will not be devalued but now he has gone back on his word, says Chuan Leekpai. (BANGKOK POST)

- Conservationists have accused Kanchanaburi governor of planning to mobilise local administrators to prevent villagers from protesting against the Yadana gas pipeline. Environmental groups and local people have voiced concern about the environmental impact of the peipeline, which will pass through lush green forests from Kanchanaburi to the power plant in Ratchaburi. (THE NATION)

- Two more judges are to face disciplinary investigations on suspicion they took bribes from Li Yun Chung, the suspected heroin trafficker. The investigations into Apichit Sombatsiri and Sitthichoke Indaraviset follow the dismissal of Somchai Udomwong, the deputy chief judge of the Criminal Court who released Li on bail. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Commerce Ministry has promptly launched measures to prevent traders from taking advantage of the baht float, which is certain to increase the inflation rate, to raise prices. The policy aims to protect consumers from traders who may use the impact of the baht's subsequent devaluation as an excuse to increase prices. (THE NATION)

- As it prepares for its Amazing Thailand campaign, the Tourism Authority of Thailand might want to consider promoting the country as "Amazing Cheap Thailand". But a major tour company operator says that while a cheaper baht might mean more foreign visitors and help the tourism industry overall, it would also cause headaches for his business. (BANGKOK POST)
